claim: For the efficient assessment for interrelated effects (EAIE) defined in Liao (2025), let \(F\) be a finite factor set with \(n=|F|\), positive maximum grades \(d_m\), and let the paper's covariant transformation be \(H(\mu)=U(\mu)+\sum_{m:\mu_m>0}\sum_{q=1}^{\mu_m}\zeta_{m,q}\). Then for every \(m\in F\) and \(1\le k\le d_m\), the EAIE obeys the exact identity \(\Psi_{m,k}(H)-\Psi_{m,k}(U)=\zeta_{m,k}+n^{-1}\sum_{j\in F}\sum_{q=1}^{d_j-1}\zeta_{j,q}\). Consequently the paper's covariant-transformation axiom holds for a given shift exactly when the total lower-grade shift is zero, and it holds for all allowed shifts if and only if every factor has only one positive grade. In every genuine multigrade domain (some \(d_j\ge2\)), Lemma 3.4 and therefore the characterization in Theorem 3.9 are false as written. A smallest two-factor witness is \(d=(2,1)\), \(U=0\), \(\zeta_{1,1}=1\) and all other shift coordinates zero: the EAIE shift is \((3/2,1/2,1/2)\), not the required \((1,0,0)\).
integrity: The source definitions, Lemma 3.4 proof, Theorem 3.9 dependency, and worked EAIE formula were read in the lawful publisher PDF.
The counterexample and coefficient identities are checked by exact rational arithmetic in verify.py.
A 2021 predecessor formula was inspected to distinguish the source-specific top-step balance from the earlier all-level balance.
scientific_limitations: The correction concerns the published EAIE formula and its COTR-based axiomatic characterization; it does not invalidate unrelated dynamic or applied conclusions that do not use this covariance statement.
Binary-grade games have no defect, and individual multigrade transformations with zero total lower-grade shift still satisfy COTR.
No uniqueness theorem for a repaired EAIE is claimed.
title: Exact covariance defect in the multigrade EAIE
